title: Kahana vs Scribd: The Playlist vs the Assigned Listen
excerpt: Scribd is audio streaming / listening at scale. Kahana is a library shelf for the audio you actually assign, plus Clubs to talk about it.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Catalog: 1.5M+ audiobooks and ebooks, plus magazines, podcasts, sheet music, and Everand Originals.
Plans (2026): Standard USD 11.99/mo (1 unlock), Plus USD 16.99/mo (3 unlocks), Deluxe USD 28.99/mo (5 unlocks), each plus 20,000+ always-available titles; 30-day free trial of Standard.
Unlock model: each unlock gives full access to one premium title; unlocked books stay available while subscribed and restore on resubscribe with the same email.

strengths.title: Multi-format catalog
strengths.detail: Audiobooks, ebooks, magazines, podcasts, sheet music, and originals in one subscription, broader than pure audiobook services.

strengths.title: Large always-available pool
strengths.detail: Credit/unlock for premium titles, plus unlimited access to a large non-premium library (20k+ titles).

strengths.title: Affordable vs many competitors
strengths.detail: Standard at USD 11.99/mo is competitive vs Audible and other audiobook subscriptions.

strengths.title: Cross-device access
strengths.detail: Web, iOS, Android, Apple Watch, and CarPlay coverage.

weaknesses.title: Credit-based access for premium titles
weaknesses.detail: Shift from “unlimited” marketing to unlocks, less appealing than true unlimited for many users.

weaknesses.title: Complexity in “what’s free”
weaknesses.detail: Distinction between unlocked and always-available titles can confuse; some content rotates in/out of unlimited availability.

weaknesses.title: Less focused on community/club features
weaknesses.detail: Primarily a content subscription, no native book/audio club tools or social features.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Scribd is audio streaming / listening at scale. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Enjoy millions of audiobooks, ebooks and more… Choose from best sellers and new releases.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Scribd side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Scribd you can use Ebook, Audio, and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with Scribd

You can use both. Scribd keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on Scribd, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
